description:
Organic Rye brings one of the most ancient and revered grains to your table. People have been cultivating this grain for over 4000 years. It spread from what the lands currently known as Turkey all over the Middle East and Europe. Organic rye berries are nutritious, delicious, and extremely good for you.


Nutrition Data
Organic rye berries contain lots of B vitamins and a variety of minerals:

Manganese
Phosphorus
Zinc
Magnesium
Iron
Copper

Organic rye berries are extremely rich in dietary fiber and protein.

Due to fiber and overall high nutritional value, organic rye berries will be a good addition to a weight management diet.


How to Cook

Cooking organic rye berries takes a while. If you soak rye grain berries overnight, they will only take about 45 minutes to cook. Otherwise, the process can take about 3 hours.

To cook organic rye berries, you’ll need to use 1 cup of water per ½ cup of dry grains. Be sure to add about ¼ teaspoon of salt.

Drain cooked organic rye berries and serve while they are still hot.

If you plan to use organic rye berries in a stew or other dish that will require them to cook further, drain them while the seeds are firm Organic rye berries, sprouted or not, should be cooked. Add this kind of sprouts to salads and sandwiches.

Organic rye berries are perfect for delicious and healthy baked goods. However, organic rye bread requires yeast to make. Don’t forget that you can mix whole berries into the dough for extra-crunch.


The most important thing is to keep them dry and cool.

description:
If you wish to exercise another grain but rice, try our Organic Spelt Berries. This delicious grain has been around for millennia; today, organic farmers are raving about wheat berries because they need fewer chemicals to grow compared to regular bread wheat. Organic Whole Spelt Berries are easy to cook and you can enjoy them in any recipe that calls for grains.

Like all whole grains, organic spelt berries are rich in fiber, B vitamins, and plant protein. Use them as a substitute for rice, even in recipes like risotto. However, unlike most whole grains, spelt wheat berries have a rich nutty flavor. Therefore, they will enhance the taste of any dish and are delicious served as a side on their own.

Please remember that Organic Whole Spelt Berries are a type of wheat; therefore, there is gluten.


How to Cook & Sprout Organic Spelt Berries

Make sure to soak Spelt Berries before cooking, overnight soaking will give you the best results, but if you can’t wait that long, leave them soaking for at least an hour.

Place the berries and water where the Spelt berries soaked in a pot and bring to a boil.

Turn down the heat and let simmer for 1-1 ½ hours.

Season with salt near the end and then drain and use the cooked grain as guided by your recipe.

When cooking spelt wheat berries, use 2 cups of water per 1 cup of grain for a chewier texture. If you need softer grain, use 3 cups of water per cup of dry spelt berries.

If you buy organic spelt berries in bulk, you might want to try not just cooking them but also grind into homemade flour or sprout. Sprouting spelt berries is the same as sprouting any other whole grain. Let them soak, cover, and then rinse and drain in a sprouter.

description: What Is White Jasmine Rice? Organic white jasmine rice is a long grain type of fragrant rice native to Thailand. It gets its name because of the subtle flowery scent and color of the polished grains, which are reminiscent of jasmine flowers. It’s the most fragrant rice of its kind and is one of the most popular in the Western world. Food To Live brings this delicious grain to your table with our Organic Jasmine Rice. You can use it to create a great variety of delicious dishes, ranging from stir-fry to pudding. Due to its pleasant flowery aroma and mildly-nutty flavor, white jasmine rice can benefit any dish when replacing other rice varieties. This particular type of grain is a traditional ingredient in Thai cuisine. It’s also a staple food in Vietnam, Cambodia, and Laos. Organic Jasmine Rice from Food To Live Food To Live Organic Jasmine Rice bulk pack contains high-quality white rice you’ll be able to enjoy in a variety of ways. This product is versatile and can be used in both sweet and savory dishes. In fact, the natural sweet flavor of organic white jasmine rice makes it a good choice for desserts. As it’s rather soft compared to other long grain rice varieties, you can make an excellent pudding with it. Difference Between Basmati and White Jasmine Rice Both basmati and jasmine rice are types of fragrant long grain rice. They are very popular in Thailand, India, China, and other Eastern countries. These grains can be used interchangeably, but white jasmine rice has a milder more flowery flavor and aroma. Basmati is a firmer, longer, and less sticky grain. It requires soaking for at least 30 minutes before cooking, while white jasmine rice can be cooked after a short rinse. The best way to cooking organic jasmine rice is steaming, but you can also boil it on the stove using 1:1 or 1:1.5 proportions of grain and water. description:
If you wish to exercise another grain but rice, try our Organic Spelt Berries. This delicious grain has been around for millennia; today, organic farmers are raving about wheat berries because they need fewer chemicals to grow compared to regular bread wheat. Organic Whole Spelt Berries are easy to cook and you can enjoy them in any recipe that calls for grains.

Like all whole grains, organic spelt berries are rich in fiber, B vitamins, and plant protein. Use them as a substitute for rice, even in recipes like risotto. However, unlike most whole grains, spelt wheat berries have a rich nutty flavor. Therefore, they will enhance the taste of any dish and are delicious served as a side on their own.

Please remember that Organic Whole Spelt Berries are a type of wheat; therefore, there is gluten.


How to Cook & Sprout Organic Spelt Berries

Make sure to soak Spelt Berries before cooking, overnight soaking will give you the best results, but if you can’t wait that long, leave them soaking for at least an hour.

Place the berries and water where the Spelt berries soaked in a pot and bring to a boil.

Turn down the heat and let simmer for 1-1 ½ hours.

Season with salt near the end and then drain and use the cooked grain as guided by your recipe.

When cooking spelt wheat berries, use 2 cups of water per 1 cup of grain for a chewier texture. If you need softer grain, use 3 cups of water per cup of dry spelt berries.

If you buy organic spelt berries in bulk, you might want to try not just cooking them but also grind into homemade flour or sprout. Sprouting spelt berries is the same as sprouting any other whole grain. Let them soak, cover, and then rinse and drain in a sprouter.

However, unlike most whole grains, spelt wheat berries have a rich nutty flavor. Therefore, they will enhance the taste of any dish and are delicious served as a side on their own.

Please remember that Organic Whole Spelt Berries are a type of wheat; therefore, there is gluten.


How to Cook & Sprout Organic Spelt Berries

Make sure to soak Spelt Berries before cooking, overnight soaking will give you the best results, but if you can’t wait that long, leave them soaking for at least an hour.

Place the berries and water where the Spelt berries soaked in a pot and bring to a boil.

Turn down the heat and let simmer for 1-1 ½ hours.

Season with salt near the end and then drain and use the cooked grain as guided by your recipe.

When cooking spelt wheat berries, use 2 cups of water per 1 cup of grain for a chewier texture. If you need softer grain, use 3 cups of water per cup of dry spelt berries.

If you buy organic spelt berries in bulk, you might want to try not just cooking them but also grind into homemade flour or sprout. Sprouting spelt berries is the same as sprouting any other whole grain. Let them soak, cover, and then rinse and drain in a sprouter.

What is Quinoa? Royal Quinoa pronunciation: keen-wa, is a "pseudo-grain" or a gluten and wheat free seed, but typically used as a grain. Royal Quinoa is rich in many nutrients and a great source of protein and fiber for those following a gluten free, vegan or vegetarian diet.

Royal Quinoa is the Smarter Rice.

Quinoa was a staple food for the Incas that dates back 3,000 years ago. It was first used for consumption in the Andean region of Bolivia. The Incas called it the “mother grain” and would host ceremonies at the first planting of the season to show respect for all the greatness that the plant provided for them.

During the European conquest, the Spanish colonist disparaged Quinoa as “food for Indians” and suppressed its cultivation. Quinoa flourished once again in the high mountains, over 4,000 meters over the sea level since it is one of few crops that survives high altitude, withstands frost, intense sun and the often-dry conditions that characterized the Andean climate.

description:
If you wish to exercise another grain but rice, try our Organic Spelt Berries. This delicious grain has been around for millennia; today, organic farmers are raving about wheat berries because they need fewer chemicals to grow compared to regular bread wheat. Organic Whole Spelt Berries are easy to cook and you can enjoy them in any recipe that calls for grains.

Like all whole grains, organic spelt berries are rich in fiber, B vitamins, and plant protein. Use them as a substitute for rice, even in recipes like risotto. However, unlike most whole grains, spelt wheat berries have a rich nutty flavor. Therefore, they will enhance the taste of any dish and are delicious served as a side on their own.

Please remember that Organic Whole Spelt Berries are a type of wheat; therefore, there is gluten.


How to Cook & Sprout Organic Spelt Berries

Make sure to soak Spelt Berries before cooking, overnight soaking will give you the best results, but if you can’t wait that long, leave them soaking for at least an hour.

Place the berries and water where the Spelt berries soaked in a pot and bring to a boil.

Turn down the heat and let simmer for 1-1 ½ hours.

Season with salt near the end and then drain and use the cooked grain as guided by your recipe.

When cooking spelt wheat berries, use 2 cups of water per 1 cup of grain for a chewier texture. If you need softer grain, use 3 cups of water per cup of dry spelt berries.

If you buy organic spelt berries in bulk, you might want to try not just cooking them but also grind into homemade flour or sprout. Sprouting spelt berries is the same as sprouting any other whole grain. Let them soak, cover, and then rinse and drain in a sprouter.

description:
Sticky rice is a starchy grain. If steamed or boiled the same way as regular rice, the grains will break down and become soft and mushy in consistency. Instead, Thai people like to cook it in such a way that the rice grains remain whole and have a firm, chewy texture. To accomplish this, the rice is soaked for several hours (4 hours or more) until the grains have absorbed enough water to cook. Then it is drained and steamed dry in a woven bamboo basket without adding any water. Though the grains remain whole, steamed sticky rice sticks together in a lump.

Does NOT contain dietary gluten; safe for gluten free diets

If you're used to long grained, please try short, it cooks better and tastes great.

description: Organic Wild Rice: Sacred Grain of Native Americans Organic wild rice is a grain that comes from North America. For many centuries it has been the staple food of many Native American peoples. Some of them considered this food sacred and it takes a special place in their cultures even today. Food To Live brings you top-quality Organic Wild Rice grown, harvested, and processed with extreme care. This highly nutritious grain is a delicacy you can enjoy in both sweet and savory dishes. There are four species of wild rice plants today and three of them are native to America. Northern Wild Rice and Wild Rice are cultivated throughout the country. Texas Wild Rice is almost extinct in the wild. This plant has taken a severe blow from the climate change as it’s rapidly losing its natural habitat. Organic wild rice is a water plant and naturally grows only in flowing water. Therefore, droughts are a fatal threat to the grains. In 1951, Gerald and James Godward proved that it can be cultivated commercially by creating the first artificial wild rice paddy. It’s thanks to them today we have wild rice fields in Minnesota and California. Manchurian rice, the only species of the plant native to China, is also almost lost to people. Unlike its North American ‘brother’ this plant is mostly cultivated for its meaty stalk. Local people enjoy it as a vegetable and often discard seeds. Food To Live Certified Organic Wild Rice for Sale Organic, non-GMO Wild Rice from Food To Live is a certified product cultivated using only natural practices. It’s grown, harvested, and processed using the traditional methods, which allow preventing contamination by chemicals. Harvesting of organic wild rice is a rather interesting but exhausting process. The seeds are literally beaten out of the plants with special knockers. Afterward, they are dried and parched. The parching process enhances the delicious flavor of this extraordinary grain.

description: What Is White Jasmine Rice? Organic white jasmine rice is a long grain type of fragrant rice native to Thailand. It gets its name because of the subtle flowery scent and color of the polished grains, which are reminiscent of jasmine flowers. It’s the most fragrant rice of its kind and is one of the most popular in the Western world. Food To Live brings this delicious grain to your table with our Organic Jasmine Rice. You can use it to create a great variety of delicious dishes, ranging from stir-fry to pudding. Due to its pleasant flowery aroma and mildly-nutty flavor, white jasmine rice can benefit any dish when replacing other rice varieties. This particular type of grain is a traditional ingredient in Thai cuisine. It’s also a staple food in Vietnam, Cambodia, and Laos. Organic Jasmine Rice from Food To Live Food To Live Organic Jasmine Rice bulk pack contains high-quality white rice you’ll be able to enjoy in a variety of ways. This product is versatile and can be used in both sweet and savory dishes. In fact, the natural sweet flavor of organic white jasmine rice makes it a good choice for desserts. As it’s rather soft compared to other long grain rice varieties, you can make an excellent pudding with it. Difference Between Basmati and White Jasmine Rice Both basmati and jasmine rice are types of fragrant long grain rice. They are very popular in Thailand, India, China, and other Eastern countries. These grains can be used interchangeably, but white jasmine rice has a milder more flowery flavor and aroma. Basmati is a firmer, longer, and less sticky grain. It requires soaking for at least 30 minutes before cooking, while white jasmine rice can be cooked after a short rinse. The best way to cooking organic jasmine rice is steaming, but you can also boil it on the stove using 1:1 or 1:1.5 proportions of grain and water. description: Organic Wild Rice: Sacred Grain of Native Americans Organic wild rice is a grain that comes from North America. Texas Wild Rice is almost extinct in the wild. This plant has taken a severe blow from the climate change as it’s rapidly losing its natural habitat. Organic wild rice is a water plant and naturally grows only in flowing water. Therefore, droughts are a fatal threat to the grains. In 1951, Gerald and James Godward proved that it can be cultivated commercially by creating the first artificial wild rice paddy. It’s thanks to them today we have wild rice fields in Minnesota and California. Manchurian rice, the only species of the plant native to China, is also almost lost to people. It’s grown, harvested, and processed using the traditional methods, which allow preventing contamination by chemicals. Harvesting of organic wild rice is a rather interesting but exhausting process. The seeds are literally beaten out of the plants with special knockers. Afterward, they are dried and parched. The parching process enhances the delicious flavor of this extraordinary grain.

description:
Organic Rye brings one of the most ancient and revered grains to your table. People have been cultivating this grain for over 4000 years. It spread from what the lands currently known as Turkey all over the Middle East and Europe. Organic rye berries are nutritious, delicious, and extremely good for you.


Nutrition Data
Organic rye berries contain lots of B vitamins and a variety of minerals:

Manganese
Phosphorus
Zinc
Magnesium
Iron
Copper

Organic rye berries are extremely rich in dietary fiber and protein.

Due to fiber and overall high nutritional value, organic rye berries will be a good addition to a weight management diet.


How to Cook

Cooking organic rye berries takes a while. If you soak rye grain berries overnight, they will only take about 45 minutes to cook. Otherwise, the process can take about 3 hours.

To cook organic rye berries, you’ll need to use 1 cup of water per ½ cup of dry grains. Be sure to add about ¼ teaspoon of salt.

Drain cooked organic rye berries and serve while they are still hot.

If you plan to use organic rye berries in a stew or other dish that will require them to cook further, drain them while the seeds are firm Organic rye berries, sprouted or not, should be cooked. If you are 100% sure that your sprouts weren’t contaminated by any bacteria, you can eat them as they are. However, rinse them extremely well and drain thoroughly.

Add this kind of sprouts to salads and sandwiches.

Cooked rye berries go well in salads, both warm and cold. They taste good with any type of vegetable.

Organic rye berries are perfect for delicious and healthy baked goods. However, organic rye bread requires yeast to make. Don’t forget that you can mix whole berries into the dough for extra-crunch.


The most important thing is to keep them dry and cool.

description: What Is White Jasmine Rice? Organic white jasmine rice is a long grain type of fragrant rice native to Thailand. It gets its name because of the subtle flowery scent and color of the polished grains, which are reminiscent of jasmine flowers. It’s the most fragrant rice of its kind and is one of the most popular in the Western world. Food To Live brings this delicious grain to your table with our Organic Jasmine Rice. You can use it to create a great variety of delicious dishes, ranging from stir-fry to pudding. Due to its pleasant flowery aroma and mildly-nutty flavor, white jasmine rice can benefit any dish when replacing other rice varieties. This particular type of grain is a traditional ingredient in Thai cuisine. It’s also a staple food in Vietnam, Cambodia, and Laos. Organic Jasmine Rice from Food To Live Food To Live Organic Jasmine Rice bulk pack contains high-quality white rice you’ll be able to enjoy in a variety of ways. This product is versatile and can be used in both sweet and savory dishes. In fact, the natural sweet flavor of organic white jasmine rice makes it a good choice for desserts. As it’s rather soft compared to other long grain rice varieties, you can make an excellent pudding with it. Difference Between Basmati and White Jasmine Rice Both basmati and jasmine rice are types of fragrant long grain rice. They are very popular in Thailand, India, China, and other Eastern countries. These grains can be used interchangeably, but white jasmine rice has a milder more flowery flavor and aroma. Basmati is a firmer, longer, and less sticky grain. It requires soaking for at least 30 minutes before cooking, while white jasmine rice can be cooked after a short rinse. The best way to cooking organic jasmine rice is steaming, but you can also boil it on the stove using 1:1 or 1:1.5 proportions of grain and water. It is then harvested with traditionally made hand tools, hand processed to remove the seed from the husk and washed and dried thoroughly. The grain itself is the smallest in the millet family, with nearly 2000 grains per gram! It is used traditionally as a staple side dish for breakfast, lunch, and dinner in a variety of preparations. Fonio is the most ancient of grains, and plays a large role in the mythology and tradition of numerous African ethnic groups. The Dogon people of Mali believe that the Universe was created from a single grain of fonio. Fonio has never been a “big name” item in the states until it was recently re-discovered by Foodies and Health Care Practitioners. Fonio does not contain any glutamine or gladding proteins which are the constituents of gluten, making this grain suitable for people with gluten intolerance. Easy to prepare: Bring water to a boil, add fonio while stirring, cover and remove from heat for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork and enjoy!

description: Organic Wild Rice: Sacred Grain of Native Americans Organic wild rice is a grain that comes from North America. For many centuries it has been the staple food of many Native American peoples. Some of them considered this food sacred and it takes a special place in their cultures even today. Food To Live brings you top-quality Organic Wild Rice grown, harvested, and processed with extreme care. This highly nutritious grain is a delicacy you can enjoy in both sweet and savory dishes. There are four species of wild rice plants today and three of them are native to America. Northern Wild Rice and Wild Rice are cultivated throughout the country. Texas Wild Rice is almost extinct in the wild. This plant has taken a severe blow from the climate change as it’s rapidly losing its natural habitat. Organic wild rice is a water plant and naturally grows only in flowing water. Therefore, droughts are a fatal threat to the grains. In 1951, Gerald and James Godward proved that it can be cultivated commercially by creating the first artificial wild rice paddy. It’s thanks to them today we have wild rice fields in Minnesota and California. Manchurian rice, the only species of the plant native to China, is also almost lost to people. Unlike its North American ‘brother’ this plant is mostly cultivated for its meaty stalk. Local people enjoy it as a vegetable and often discard seeds. It’s grown, harvested, and processed using the traditional methods, which allow preventing contamination by chemicals. Harvesting of organic wild rice is a rather interesting but exhausting process. The seeds are literally beaten out of the plants with special knockers. Afterward, they are dried and parched. The parching process enhances the delicious flavor of this extraordinary grain.

description:
Long grain sticky rice, also known as glutinous rice, is one of the delicacies of Asian cuisine. In fact, long grain sticky rice is most commonly used in the famous Thai dish "sticky rice and mango," while short grain sticky rice is used quite often in Japanese sushi.

Now, what makes sticky rice different from regular white rice? Where does it originate from? And where does it get its stickiness? In fact, the stickiness comes from a low amount of the starch amylase but extra amylopectin, and this also gives the rice a sweet flavor that makes it the most desired alternative to regular white rice.

Our long grain sticky rice is cultivated in the wetlands of California. Because of California's low humidity and close proximity to the ocean, it provides the most ideal climate necessary to produce the best quality rice. In fact, California is known to produce the largest amounts of rice crops in the world.

Unlike most crops, rice is an aquatic plant that needs continues watering. California's wetland environment is ideal because it enhances weed control and minimizes the need for additional fertilizers.

description: Brown rice is a type of cereal, which got its name due to its dark color. Grains do not undergo deep processing, and an outer coating remains rice bran, which has a brown tint. Brown rice is more nutritious than white. It has a nutty flavor because the bran is “attached” to the grains and contains oils with unsaturated fats. Calorie of Organic Long Grain Brown Rice is not small. In general, it is 100 kilocalories per 1 ounce. But in the form of a cooked, the number of calories decreases almost three times. It allows you to get enough without a large number of calories, and the body will receive a mass of nutrients. Organic Long Grain Brown Rice contains a large number of beneficial trace elements and vitamins. Brown Rice contains on average 3-3.5 times more protein than white rice, and 12 times more fiber. This rice contains a wide range of B vitamins, as well as trace elements such as potassium, phosphorus, and magnesium. It also contains selenium, zinc and vitamin E. How to Cook 1. Rinse the cereal in cold water until it is clear. 2. Soak it for several hours in cold water (or overnight). 3. Transfer the prepared rice to the cooking pot and pour cold water at the rate of 1 cup of cereal to 2.5-3 cups of water, add a teaspoon of salt and bring to a boil. 4. On high heat rice cook for 5-10 minutes under a tightly closed lid. 5. Remove from heat, rinse in cold water. 6. Add rice to cold water again and cook for another 15 minutes after boiling, 7. Remove from heat and wrap in a blanket so that the rice has reached readiness. To keep brown the rice longer, put it to an airtight container and store in a cool and dark place. description: What Is Brown Basmati Rice? Billions of people all over the world eat rice and quite a number of them does so daily as it’s a staple food for the entirety of Asia. There are many varieties of this grain and each of them has its own unique nutritional makeup and flavor. The versatility of it is increased further by the many uses of rice, which range from cooking to cosmetics. All in all, this grain is fantastic in all its forms, but brown basmati rice takes a special place among them due to the combination of its nutritional value and a unique flavor. This particular species has been cultivated for many centuries. There are mentions of it in the ancient Indian literature, and it’s safe to assume that it has been known to our ancestors from much earlier. Trading caravans brought basmati rice to the Middle East. It has become so loved there that now it’s one of the major ingredients used in many local dishes. Until today India and Pakistan remain the main producers of basmati rice. This encompasses both of its varieties, white and brown, which differ by the way the kernel is processed. The thing that makes brown basmati rice stand out among the other types of this grain is its elevated fiber content and a truly unique aroma. The latter is caused by the fact that it contains 12 times more the chemical that gives rice its natural smell as compared to most other species of its group.

description:
If you wish to exercise another grain but rice, try our Organic Spelt Berries. This delicious grain has been around for millennia; today, organic farmers are raving about wheat berries because they need fewer chemicals to grow compared to regular bread wheat. Organic Whole Spelt Berries are easy to cook and you can enjoy them in any recipe that calls for grains.

Like all whole grains, organic spelt berries are rich in fiber, B vitamins, and plant protein. Use them as a substitute for rice, even in recipes like risotto. However, unlike most whole grains, spelt wheat berries have a rich nutty flavor. Therefore, they will enhance the taste of any dish and are delicious served as a side on their own.

Please remember that Organic Whole Spelt Berries are a type of wheat; therefore, there is gluten.


How to Cook & Sprout Organic Spelt Berries

Make sure to soak Spelt Berries before cooking, overnight soaking will give you the best results, but if you can’t wait that long, leave them soaking for at least an hour.

Place the berries and water where the Spelt berries soaked in a pot and bring to a boil.

Turn down the heat and let simmer for 1-1 ½ hours.

Season with salt near the end and then drain and use the cooked grain as guided by your recipe.

When cooking spelt wheat berries, use 2 cups of water per 1 cup of grain for a chewier texture. If you need softer grain, use 3 cups of water per cup of dry spelt berries.

If you buy organic spelt berries in bulk, you might want to try not just cooking them but also grind into homemade flour or sprout. Sprouting spelt berries is the same as sprouting any other whole grain. Let them soak, cover, and then rinse and drain in a sprouter.

NorQuin, based in Saskatchewan Canada, is a technology driven, vertically integrated supplier of quinoa and quinoa derivative products. What Is Quinoa?

Quinoa (Keen-wa) is an amino acid (protein) rich seed that has a fluffy, creamy, sightly crunchy texture and a somewhat nutty flavor when cooked. description:
Millet grain doesn’t have any gluten contains lots of essential vitamins, minerals, and fiber. This grain has been a staple in many cuisines for years. And while it’s not as popular as rice, wheat, or oats, it’s gaining more recognition all over the world. The reason for this is simple; millet is delicious, nutritious, and very easy to cook.

Food to Live While Millet, also known as White Proso, is the most popular type of this grain. There are about 500 species of plants that are considered millet, but only a few of them used as food. Pearl and foxglove millet also are popular crops. All types of millet are similar in taste and nutritional value. However, experts believe that white millet was domesticated first. Presumably, as a crop, it dates back to around 10,000 BC.


How to Cook White Millet Proso

Hulled whole grain millet has a rich nutty and mildly sweet flavor. Because of this, the grain tastes fantastic in a variety of sweet and savory dishes. In fact, replacing grains in the recipe with this one can make the dish taste much better.

There are many ways to use millet; it is easy to cook; hulled millet doesn’t need pre-soaking and cooks in less than 30 minutes.

Try to roast dry grain in a pan or skillet for about 5 minutes and add water or broth. Use two parts of liquid per 1 part of the grain. Increase the amount of water to three parts if you want to enjoy pure millet taste in a porridge.

After adding water, bring the pot to a boil and turn down the heat to simmer right away. Do not often stir as hulled millet grain is very tender. Let it simmer for about fifteen minutes, so all water is absorbed. Then, let the pot sit covered for ten minutes and fluff up the cooked grain using a fork.

This rice contains a wide range of B vitamins, as well as trace elements such as potassium, phosphorus, and magnesium. It also contains selenium, zinc and vitamin E. How to Cook 1. Rinse the cereal in cold water until it is clear. 2. Soak it for several hours in cold water (or overnight). 3. Transfer the prepared rice to the cooking pot and pour cold water at the rate of 1 cup of cereal to 2.5-3 cups of water, add a teaspoon of salt and bring to a boil. 4. On high heat rice cook for 5-10 minutes under a tightly closed lid. 5. Remove from heat, rinse in cold water. 6. Add rice to cold water again and cook for another 15 minutes after boiling, 7. Remove from heat and wrap in a blanket so that the rice has reached readiness. To keep brown the rice longer, put it to an airtight container and store in a cool and dark place. The versatility of it is increased further by the many uses of rice, which range from cooking to cosmetics. This particular species has been cultivated for many centuries. description:
Couscous Pearls, also known as Israeli Couscous, are small balls of toasted semolina flour. 

In Israel they are called Ptitim. 

During 1949 - 1959, Israel went through an austerity period during which food and other resources were rationed. Rice, a dietary staple, was scarce, and there was a need to come up with an alternative food source. 

Israel's first Prime Minister, David Ben-Gurion, asked the founders of a local food company to create a wheat-based substitute for rice. 

The result was tiny, toasted pasta made from hard wheat flour. It was an instant success with the people, and they gave it the nickname ‚"Ben-Gurion's Rice." 

Today, Israeli couscous remains a staple food in Jerusalem and is enjoyed by people in many places around the world. Bob's Red Mill Traditional Pearl Couscous has a unique nutty flavor and pleasantly chewy texture that pairs exceptionally well with your favorite sauces, so it can be a great alternative to traditional pastas and rice. 

Use Traditional Pearl Couscous as a bed for stew, meat or vegetables, or try it with your favorite pasta sauce. Add Israeli couscous to soups, salads and pilafs for a new twist on old stand-bys. 

Like rice, couscous pearls will absorb the flavors of whatever spices or sauce you are using. Using pearl couscous, quick and easy main dishes and salads are just minutes away.

description:
Millet grain doesn’t have any gluten contains lots of essential vitamins, minerals, and fiber. This grain has been a staple in many cuisines for years. And while it’s not as popular as rice, wheat, or oats, it’s gaining more recognition all over the world. The reason for this is simple; millet is delicious, nutritious, and very easy to cook.

Food to Live While Millet, also known as White Proso, is the most popular type of this grain. There are about 500 species of plants that are considered millet, but only a few of them used as food. Pearl and foxglove millet also are popular crops. All types of millet are similar in taste and nutritional value. However, experts believe that white millet was domesticated first. Presumably, as a crop, it dates back to around 10,000 BC.


How to Cook White Millet Proso

Hulled whole grain millet has a rich nutty and mildly sweet flavor. Because of this, the grain tastes fantastic in a variety of sweet and savory dishes. In fact, replacing grains in the recipe with this one can make the dish taste much better.

There are many ways to use millet; it is easy to cook; hulled millet doesn’t need pre-soaking and cooks in less than 30 minutes.

Try to roast dry grain in a pan or skillet for about 5 minutes and add water or broth. Use two parts of liquid per 1 part of the grain. Increase the amount of water to three parts if you want to enjoy pure millet taste in a porridge.

After adding water, bring the pot to a boil and turn down the heat to simmer right away. Do not often stir as hulled millet grain is very tender. Let it simmer for about fifteen minutes, so all water is absorbed. Then, let the pot sit covered for ten minutes and fluff up the cooked grain using a fork.

description: Brown rice is a type of cereal, which got its name due to its dark color. Grains do not undergo deep processing, and an outer coating remains rice bran, which has a brown tint. Brown rice is more nutritious than white. It has a nutty flavor because the bran is “attached” to the grains and contains oils with unsaturated fats. Calorie of Organic Long Grain Brown Rice is not small. In general, it is 100 kilocalories per 1 ounce. But in the form of a cooked, the number of calories decreases almost three times. It allows you to get enough without a large number of calories, and the body will receive a mass of nutrients. Organic Long Grain Brown Rice contains a large number of beneficial trace elements and vitamins. Brown Rice contains on average 3-3.5 times more protein than white rice, and 12 times more fiber. This rice contains a wide range of B vitamins, as well as trace elements such as potassium, phosphorus, and magnesium. It also contains selenium, zinc and vitamin E. How to Cook 1. Rinse the cereal in cold water until it is clear. 2. Soak it for several hours in cold water (or overnight). 3. Make sure to soak Spelt Berries before cooking, overnight soaking will give you the best results, but if you can’t wait that long, leave them soaking for at least an hour.

Turn down the heat and let simmer for 1-1 ½ hours.

Season with salt near the end and then drain and use the cooked grain as guided by your recipe.

When cooking spelt wheat berries, use 2 cups of water per 1 cup of grain for a chewier texture. If you need softer grain, use 3 cups of water per cup of dry spelt berries.

If you buy organic spelt berries in bulk, you might want to try not just cooking them but also grind into homemade flour or sprout. Sprouting spelt berries is the same as sprouting any other whole grain. Let them soak, cover, and then rinse and drain in a sprouter.

description:
Millet grain doesn’t have any gluten contains lots of essential vitamins, minerals, and fiber. This grain has been a staple in many cuisines for years. And while it’s not as popular as rice, wheat, or oats, it’s gaining more recognition all over the world. The reason for this is simple; millet is delicious, nutritious, and very easy to cook.

Food to Live While Millet, also known as White Proso, is the most popular type of this grain. There are about 500 species of plants that are considered millet, but only a few of them used as food. Pearl and foxglove millet also are popular crops. All types of millet are similar in taste and nutritional value. However, experts believe that white millet was domesticated first. Presumably, as a crop, it dates back to around 10,000 BC.


How to Cook White Millet Proso

Hulled whole grain millet has a rich nutty and mildly sweet flavor. Because of this, the grain tastes fantastic in a variety of sweet and savory dishes. In fact, replacing grains in the recipe with this one can make the dish taste much better.

There are many ways to use millet; it is easy to cook; hulled millet doesn’t need pre-soaking and cooks in less than 30 minutes.

Try to roast dry grain in a pan or skillet for about 5 minutes and add water or broth. Use two parts of liquid per 1 part of the grain. Increase the amount of water to three parts if you want to enjoy pure millet taste in a porridge.

After adding water, bring the pot to a boil and turn down the heat to simmer right away. Do not often stir as hulled millet grain is very tender. Let it simmer for about fifteen minutes, so all water is absorbed. Then, let the pot sit covered for ten minutes and fluff up the cooked grain using a fork.

description: Fonio is one of the preeminent African superfoods and holds an honored place in West African, and particularly Sahel, culture. Earths Goodness fonio is grown in the Sahel area that borders the Sahara Desert, and it does well in dry and grassy savannah as well as in richer climates. Earths Goodness fonio’s beloved place on West African plates is just as well, because the grain is indubitably good for us. description: What Is White Jasmine Rice? Organic white jasmine rice is a long grain type of fragrant rice native to Thailand. It gets its name because of the subtle flowery scent and color of the polished grains, which are reminiscent of jasmine flowers. It’s the most fragrant rice of its kind and is one of the most popular in the Western world. Food To Live brings this delicious grain to your table with our Organic Jasmine Rice. You can use it to create a great variety of delicious dishes, ranging from stir-fry to pudding. Due to its pleasant flowery aroma and mildly-nutty flavor, white jasmine rice can benefit any dish when replacing other rice varieties. This particular type of grain is a traditional ingredient in Thai cuisine. It’s also a staple food in Vietnam, Cambodia, and Laos. Organic Jasmine Rice from Food To Live Food To Live Organic Jasmine Rice bulk pack contains high-quality white rice you’ll be able to enjoy in a variety of ways. This product is versatile and can be used in both sweet and savory dishes. In fact, the natural sweet flavor of organic white jasmine rice makes it a good choice for desserts. As it’s rather soft compared to other long grain rice varieties, you can make an excellent pudding with it. Difference Between Basmati and White Jasmine Rice Both basmati and jasmine rice are types of fragrant long grain rice. They are very popular in Thailand, India, China, and other Eastern countries. These grains can be used interchangeably, but white jasmine rice has a milder more flowery flavor and aroma. Basmati is a firmer, longer, and less sticky grain. It requires soaking for at least 30 minutes before cooking, while white jasmine rice can be cooked after a short rinse. The best way to cooking organic jasmine rice is steaming, but you can also boil it on the stove using 1:1 or 1:1.5 proportions of grain and water. title: Jovial Foods Organic Einkorn Wheat Berries, 16.0-Ounce
bullet_point: [Our organic einkorn wheat berries are grown and packaged on one secluded and pristine farm in Tuscany, Wheat berries are the whole grain or seed that are later milled to flour, Einkorn is the first and most ancient variety of wheat, grows inside an outer husk]
description:
Our organic einkorn wheat berries are grown and packaged on one secluded and pristine farm in Tuscany. Wheat berries are the whole grain or seed that are later milled to flour. Einkorn is the first and most ancient variety of wheat, grows inside an outer husk. At the farm, we carefully clean the husk but do not polish or pearl the grain, so you are eating 100% of the bran and germ. Wheat berries can be cooked like brown rice in just a half an hour, prepared like risotto, eaten in soups, cold in salads or cracked in a blender and eaten like porridge oats. For the absolute freshest 100% whole einkorn flour, you can use a grain mill to grind the berries as needed. With 9g of protein, 4g of fiber and an abundance of B vitamins per serving, you will really feel sustained and energized by a wholesome meal of ancient einkorn. Einkorn wheat berries should be stored properly to ensure freshness. The most prudent step to proper storage is estimating and storing only what you will be using over a 1-2 month period of time and not opening more than that amount. Therefore, if you bake infrequently, it is not a good idea to buy a bulk amount. It's best to buy smaller amounts more frequently and then always work with the freshest ingredients. Here is how you can store your wheat berries for maximum freshness: If einkorn wheat berries are packaged in an airtight bag, they will stay fresh until the expiration date on the package. Once opened, wheat berries can be stored at room temperature in an airtight container away from direct sunlight or sources of heat for 60 days. For longer storage or if the temperatures in your kitchen are frequently above 75F, refrigeration in an airtight container is recommended.

Nuestras bayas orgánicas de trigo einkorn se cultivan y envasan en una granja aislada y prístina en la Toscana. Las bayas de trigo son el grano entero o la semilla que más tarde se molen a la harina. Einkorn es la primera y más antigua variedad de trigo, crece dentro de una cáscara externa. En la granja, limpiamos cuidadosamente la cáscara, pero no pulimos ni perlamos el grano, por lo que estás comiendo el 100% del salvado y el germen. Las bayas de trigo se pueden cocinar como el arroz integral en solo media hora, preparadas como risotto, comidas en sopas, frías en ensaladas o agrietadas en una licuadora y se comen como avena de avena. Para la harina completa 100% más fresca absoluta einkorn, puede utilizar un molino de grano para moler las bayas según sea necesario. Con 0.32 oz de proteína, 0.14 oz de fibra y una abundancia de vitaminas B por porción, realmente se sentirá sostenido y energizado por una comida saludable de la antigua einkorn. Las bayas de trigo Einkorn deben almacenarse adecuadamente para garantizar la frescura. El paso más prudente para el almacenamiento adecuado es estimar y almacenar solo lo que va a utilizar durante un período de 1-2 meses y no abrir más de esa cantidad. Por lo tanto, si hornea con poca frecuencia, no es una buena idea comprar una cantidad a granel. Lo mejor es comprar cantidades más pequeñas con más frecuencia y luego siempre trabajar con los ingredientes más frescos. Aquí es cómo puede almacenar sus bayas de trigo para obtener la máxima frescura: Si las bayas de trigo einkorn se empaquetan en una bolsa hermética, se mantendrán frescas hasta la fecha de caducidad del paquete. Una vez abiertas, las bayas de trigo se pueden almacenar a temperatura ambiente en un recipiente hermético lejos de la luz solar directa o fuentes de calor durante 60 días. Para un almacenamiento más largo o si las temperaturas en su cocina son frecuentemente superiores a 75F, se recomienda la refrigeración en un recipiente hermético.

Unsere Bio Einkorn Weizenbeeren werden auf einer abgelegenen und makellosen Farm in der Toskana angebaut und verpackt. Weizenbeeren sind das ganze Getreide oder Samen, die später zu Mehl gemahlen werden. Einkorn ist die erste und älteste Weizensorte, wächst in einer Außenschale. Auf dem Bauernhof reinigen wir die Schalen sorgfältig, aber polieren oder perlen die Körnung, so dass Sie 100% der Kleie und Keime essen. Weizenbeeren können wie brauner Reis in nur einer halben Stunde gekocht werden, wie Risotto zubereitet, in Suppen gegessen werden, kalt in Salaten oder in einem Mixer zerbrochen und wie Brei Haferflocken gegessen werden. Für das absolut frischeste 100% ganze Einkornmehl können Sie die Beeren je nach Bedarf mit einer Getreidemühle mahlen. Mit 9 g Protein, 4 g Ballaststoffen und einer Fülle von B-Vitaminen pro Portion, werden Sie sich wirklich von einer gesunden Mahlzeit des alten Einkorns nachhaltig und energetisiert fühlen. Einkorn Weizenbeeren sollten ordnungsgemäß gelagert werden, um Frische zu gewährleisten. Der umsichtige Schritt zur ordnungsgemäßen Lagerung ist die Schätzung und Speicherung nur das, was Sie über einen Zeitraum von 1-2 Monaten verwenden und nicht mehr als diese Menge öffnen. Wenn Sie also selten backen, ist es keine gute Idee, eine große Menge zu kaufen. Am besten kleinere Mengen häufiger kaufen und dann immer mit den frischesten Zutaten arbeiten. So können Sie Ihre Weizenbeeren für maximale Frische aufbewahren: Wenn Einkorn Weizenbeeren in einem luftdichten Beutel verpackt sind, bleiben sie bis zum Ablaufdatum auf der Verpackung frisch. Nach dem Öffnen können Weizenbeeren bei Raumtemperatur in einem luftdichten Behälter aufbewahrt werden, der vor direkter Sonneneinstrahlung oder Wärmequellen geschützt ist. Für eine längere Lagerung oder wenn die Temperaturen in Ihrer Küche häufig über 20 °C liegen, wird die Kühlung in einem luftdichten Behälter empfohlen.

Einkorn הוא המגוון הראשון והעתיק ביותר של חיטה, גדל בתוך קליפה חיצונית. בחווה, אנו מנקים בקפידה את הקליפה אך לא מלטשים או מפנינים את התבואה, כך שאתם אוכלים 100% מהסובין והחיידקים. ניתן לבשל גרגרי חיטה כמו אורז חום תוך חצי שעה, להכין כמו ריזוטו, לאכול במרקים, קר בסלטים או לסדוק בבלנדר ולאכול כמו שיבולת שועל דייסה. עבור קמח einkorn מלא לחלוטין 100% טרי, אתה יכול להשתמש טחנת דגנים כדי לטחון את הגרגרים לפי הצורך. עם 9 גרם של חלבון, 4 גרם של סיבים ושפע של ויטמיני B למנה, אתם באמת תרגישו מתמשכת ואנרגטית על ידי ארוחה בריאה של einkorn עתיק. Einkorn חיטה גרגרי יער צריכים להיות מאוחסנים כראוי כדי להבטיח רעננות. הצעד הנבון ביותר לאחסון נכון הוא הערכת ואחסון רק מה שתשתמשו במשך תקופה של 1-2 חודשים ולא תפתח יותר מכמות זו. לכן, אם אתם אופים לעתים רחוקות, זה לא רעיון טוב לקנות כמות גדולה. מומלץ לקנות כמויות קטנות יותר בתדירות גבוהה יותר ואז תמיד לעבוד עם המרכיבים הטריים ביותר. כך תוכלו לאחסן את גרגרי החיטה שלכם לרעננות מקסימלית: אם גרגרי החיטה של einkorn ארוזים בשקית אטומה, הם יישארו טריים עד תאריך התפוגה על החבילה. לאחר הפתיחה, ניתן לאחסן את גרגרי החיטה בטמפרטורת החדר במיכל אטום הרחק מאור שמש ישיר או ממקורות חום במשך 60 יום. לאחסון ארוך יותר או אם הטמפרטורות במטבח שלכם הן לעתים קרובות מעל 75 מעלות צלזיוס, מומלץ להשתמש בקירור במיכל אטום.

يتم زراعة وتعبئة توت القمح العضوي الخاص بنا في مزرعة واحدة معزولة ونقية في توسكاني. توت القمح هو الحبوب الكاملة أو البذور التي يتم طحنها لاحقًا إلى الطحين. إينكرن هي المجموعة الأولى والأقدم من القمح، تنمو داخل قشر خارجي. في المزرعة، نقوم بتنظيف القشور بعناية ولكن لا تلمع أو تلمع الحبوب ، لذلك فأنت تأكل 100% من النخالة والجراثيم. يمكن طهي التوت القمح مثل الأرز البني في نصف ساعة فقط، وهو جاهز مثل الريسوتو، ويمكن أكله في الحساء، أو بارد في السلطة أو تشققه في خلاط ويأكله مثل الشوفان العصيدة. للحصول على أكثر طعامًا وانتعاشًا على الإطلاق بنسبة 100%، يمكنك استخدام مطحنة حبوب لطحن التوت حسب الحاجة. مع 9 غرام من البروتين و4 غرام من الألياف ووفرة من فيتامينات بي لكل وجبة، ستشعر حقًا باستدامة ونشاط من وجبة صحية من الأينكورن القديمة. يجب تخزين توت القمح من إينككورن بشكل صحيح لضمان النضارة. الخطوة الأكثر حكمة للتخزين المناسب هي تقدير وتخزين ما ستستخدمه أكثر من شهر إلى شهرين ولا تفتح أكثر من تلك الكمية. لذلك، إذا كنت تخبز بشكل متكرر، فليست فكرة جيدة أن تشتري كمية كبيرة. من الأفضل شراء كميات أصغر بشكل متكرر ثم العمل دائمًا مع المكونات الأكثر نضارة. إليك كيفية تخزين توت القمح الخاص بك للحصول على أقصى قدر من النضارة: إذا تم تعبئة توت القمح من إينككورن في حقيبة محكمة الإغلاق، فسيظل منتعشًا حتى تاريخ انتهاء الصلاحية على العبوة. بمجرد فتحه، يمكن تخزين توت القمح في درجة حرارة الغرفة في حاوية محكمة الغلق بعيدًا عن أشعة الشمس المباشرة أو مصادر الحرارة لمدة 60 يومًا. للتخزين لفترة أطول أو إذا كانت درجات الحرارة في مطبخك أكثر من 75 درجة فهرنهايت، يوصى بالتبريد في حاوية محكمة الإغلاق.

Nossas bagas de trigo einkorn orgânicas são cultivadas e embaladas em uma fazenda isolada e imaculada na Toscana. As bagas de trigo são o grão integral ou semente que são mais tarde moídas para farinha. Einkorn é a primeira e mais antiga variedade de trigo, cresce dentro de uma casca externa. Na fazenda, limpamos cuidadosamente a casca, mas não polimos nem perolamos o grão, então você está comendo 100% do farelo e do germe. As bagas de trigo podem ser cozidas como arroz integral em apenas meia hora, preparadas como risoto, comidas em sopas, frias em saladas ou rachadas em um liquidificador e comidas como aveia de mingau. Para a farinha 100% mais fresca, você pode usar um moedor de grãos para moer as frutas conforme necessário. Com 9 g de proteína, 4 g de fibra e uma abundância de vitaminas B por porção, você realmente se sentirá sustentado e energizado por uma refeição saudável de einkorn antiga. As bagas de trigo Einkorn devem ser armazenadas adequadamente para garantir o frescor. O passo mais prudente para o armazenamento adequado é estimar e armazenar apenas o que você usará durante um período de 1 a 2 meses e não abrir mais do que essa quantidade. Portanto, se você assar com pouco frequência, não é uma boa ideia comprar uma quantidade a granel. É melhor comprar quantidades menores com mais frequência e depois sempre trabalhar com os ingredientes mais frescos. Aqui está como você pode guardar suas bagas de trigo para o máximo de frescura: Se as bagas de trigo einkorn forem embaladas em uma bolsa hermética, elas permanecerão frescas até a data de validade no pacote. Uma vez abertas, as bagas de trigo podem ser armazenadas em temperatura ambiente em um recipiente hermético longe da luz solar direta ou fontes de calor por 60 dias. Para armazenamento mais longo ou se as temperaturas na sua cozinha forem frequentemente acima de 22 °C, recomenda-se a refrigeração em um recipiente hermético.

我们的有机乌红麦浆果是在托斯卡纳一个偏僻原始农场种植和包装。 小麦浆果是全谷物或种子,后来被研磨成面粉。 Einkorn 是第一种也是最古老的小麦品种,生长在外壳中。 在农场，我们小心清洁外壳，但不会抛光或珍珠颗粒，所以您正在吃100％的麸皮和细菌。 小麦浆果可以在半小时内像糙米一样烹制,如意大利烩饭,汤中吃,沙拉冷或搅拌机破裂,像粥燕麦一样吃。 为了获得绝对新鲜的100%全乌红面粉,您可以根据需要使用谷物研磨器研磨浆果。 每份含有9克蛋白质,4克纤维和丰富的B族维生素,你会感受到一顿有益健康的古代爱肯恩膳食带来的持续和充满活力。 Einkorn 小麦浆果应适当存放,以确保新鲜度。 正确存储最谨慎的步骤是估计和存储您在 1-2 个月以上的时间内使用的东西,并且开口不大于该量。 因此,如果您不频繁烘焙,购买大量量是不好主意。 最好经常购买少量产品,然后始终配合新鲜的成分。 您可以储存小麦浆果以获得最大的新鲜度:如果Einkorn 小麦浆果包装在密封袋中,它们将保持新鲜,直到包装上的有效期。 打开后,小麦浆果可以在常温下存放在密封容器中,远离阳光直射或热量源60天。 为了延长存储时间,或厨房温度经常高于 75 华氏度,建议在密封容器中冷藏。

我們的有機玉米小麥漿果在托斯卡納的一個寧靜原始農場種植和包裝。 小麥漿果是後來研磨成麵粉的全穀物或種子。 Einkorn 是第一種也是最古老的小麥品種,生長在外殼殼內。 在農場,我們仔細清潔殼,但不要拋光或珍珠穀物,所以你正在吃 100% 的麩皮和細菌。 小麥漿果可以在半小時內像糙米一樣烹製,如意大利飯、湯中食用、沙拉冷或攪拌機破裂,然後像燕麥一樣食用。 對於絕對新鮮的 100% 全einkorn 麵粉,您可以根據需要使用穀物研磨漿果。 每份含 9 公克蛋白質、4 公克纖維和豐富的 B 維他命,您會感受到透過一頓健康古老的洋蔥來維持和活力。 Einkorn 小麥漿果應妥善儲存,以確保新鮮。 正確儲存最謹慎的步驟是僅估算和儲存您使用 1-2 個月的時間,而不會打開超過該數量。 因此,如果您不常烘烤,購買大量量不是一個好主意。 ​ 最好更頻繁地購買少量,然後始終使用最新鮮的成分。 ​ 以下是如何儲存小麥漿果以獲得最大新鮮度:如果 einkorn 小麥漿果包裝在密封袋中,它們將保持新鮮,直到包裝上的過期日。 打開後,小麥漿果可在室溫下儲存在一個密封容器中,遠離陽光直射或熱源,持續 60 天。 為了更長時間儲存,或如果廚房的溫度常高於華氏 75 度,建議在氣密容器中冷藏。

우리의 유기농 einkorn 밀 열매는 토스카나의 한적한 깨끗한 농장에서 재배되고 포장됩니다. 밀 열매는 나중에 밀가루로 가공되는 통곡물 또는 씨앗입니다. Einkorn은 바깥쪽 껍질 안에서 자라는 밀의 첫 번째이자 가장 오래된 품종입니다. 농장에서는 껍질을 조심스럽게 닦아내지만 곡물을 연마하거나 진주하지 않으므로 밀기울과 세균의 100%를 먹습니다. 밀 베리는 현미처럼 30분 만에 요리할 수 있으며, 리조토처럼 준비하거나, 수프에 먹거나, 샐러드를 차갑거나 블렌더로 금이 간 후 죽귀리처럼 먹을 수 있습니다. 절대적으로 신선한 100% 전체 einkorn 가루를 위해 곡물 분쇄기를 사용하여 필요에 따라 열매를 갈 수 있습니다. 9g의 단백질, 4g의 섬유질과 풍부한 비타민 B가 함유되어 있어 고대 유콘의 건강한 식사로 지속되고 활력을 느낄 수 있습니다. Einkorn 밀 열매는 신선함을 보장하기 위해 제대로 보관해야 합니다. 적절한 보관을 위한 가장 신중한 단계는 1-2개월 동안 사용할 것만을 추정하고 저장하는 것이며 그 양을 초과하지 않는 것입니다. 따라서, 자주 굽는 경우 대량 구매하는 것은 좋지 않습니다. 소량을 더 자주 구입하고 항상 신선한 재료를 사용하는 것이 가장 좋습니다. 최대 신선도를 위해 밀 베리를 보관할 수 있는 방법은 다음과 같습니다. einkorn 밀 열매가 밀폐 백에 포장되면 포장의 만료 날짜까지 신선하게 유지됩니다. 열면 밀베리를 실온에서 직사광선이나 열원이 닿지 않는 밀폐 용기에 60일 동안 보관할 수 있습니다. 더 오래 보관하거나 주방의 온도가 75F 이상인 경우 밀폐 용기에 냉장 보관하는 것이 좋습니다.

description:
Long grain sticky rice, also known as glutinous rice, is one of the delicacies of Asian cuisine. In fact, long grain sticky rice is most commonly used in the famous Thai dish "sticky rice and mango," while short grain sticky rice is used quite often in Japanese sushi.

Now, what makes sticky rice different from regular white rice? Where does it originate from? And where does it get its stickiness? In fact, the stickiness comes from a low amount of the starch amylase but extra amylopectin, and this also gives the rice a sweet flavor that makes it the most desired alternative to regular white rice.

Our long grain sticky rice is cultivated in the wetlands of California. Because of California's low humidity and close proximity to the ocean, it provides the most ideal climate necessary to produce the best quality rice. In fact, California is known to produce the largest amounts of rice crops in the world.

Unlike most crops, rice is an aquatic plant that needs continues watering. California's wetland environment is ideal because it enhances weed control and minimizes the need for additional fertilizers.

description: Brown rice is a type of cereal, which got its name due to its dark color. Grains do not undergo deep processing, and an outer coating remains rice bran, which has a brown tint. Brown rice is more nutritious than white. It has a nutty flavor because the bran is “attached” to the grains and contains oils with unsaturated fats. Calorie of Organic Long Grain Brown Rice is not small. In general, it is 100 kilocalories per 1 ounce. But in the form of a cooked, the number of calories decreases almost three times. It allows you to get enough without a large number of calories, and the body will receive a mass of nutrients. Organic Long Grain Brown Rice contains a large number of beneficial trace elements and vitamins. Brown Rice contains on average 3-3.5 times more protein than white rice, and 12 times more fiber. This rice contains a wide range of B vitamins, as well as trace elements such as potassium, phosphorus, and magnesium. It also contains selenium, zinc and vitamin E. How to Cook 1. Rinse the cereal in cold water until it is clear. 2. Soak it for several hours in cold water (or overnight). 3. Transfer the prepared rice to the cooking pot and pour cold water at the rate of 1 cup of cereal to 2.5-3 cups of water, add a teaspoon of salt and bring to a boil. 4. On high heat rice cook for 5-10 minutes under a tightly closed lid. 5. Remove from heat, rinse in cold water. 6. Add rice to cold water again and cook for another 15 minutes after boiling, 7. Remove from heat and wrap in a blanket so that the rice has reached readiness. To keep brown the rice longer, put it to an airtight container and store in a cool and dark place. description:
Long grain sticky rice, also known as glutinous rice, is one of the delicacies of Asian cuisine. In fact, long grain sticky rice is most commonly used in the famous Thai dish "sticky rice and mango," while short grain sticky rice is used quite often in Japanese sushi.

Now, what makes sticky rice different from regular white rice? Where does it originate from? And where does it get its stickiness? In fact, the stickiness comes from a low amount of the starch amylase but extra amylopectin, and this also gives the rice a sweet flavor that makes it the most desired alternative to regular white rice.

Our long grain sticky rice is cultivated in the wetlands of California. Because of California's low humidity and close proximity to the ocean, it provides the most ideal climate necessary to produce the best quality rice. In fact, California is known to produce the largest amounts of rice crops in the world.

Unlike most crops, rice is an aquatic plant that needs continues watering. California's wetland environment is ideal because it enhances weed control and minimizes the need for additional fertilizers.

Quinoa flour can also be added directly to soups and stews as a thickening agent, or used like a protein powder in smoothies and shakes., Buckwheat is one of the favorite flours it is used to make buckwheat soufflés, biscuits, scones, sponge cakes, butter cakes, gingerbread, cookies, and crackers., Buckwheat adds a can’t-put-your-finger-on-it heartiness to these biscuits. Apples tease out the inherent sweetness of nutty buckwheat, but can be happily subbed with dried cherries., Tapioca flour is virtually tasteless and odourless but is used to achieve a spongy, light and fluffy texture in baked goods or to make crispy pie crusts and pizzas.]
description:
Quinoa flour is made by grinding quinoa seeds to a fine consistency. It looks and feels like all-purpose wheat flour and is easily adapted to a broad range of baking recipes, from desserts to muffins to breads. Quinoa flour has a very bold flavor, almost grass-like and a little bitter, that sometimes can overpower a recipe.

►Buckwheat is a short-season crop that grows well in low-fertility or acidic soils; too much fertilizer – especially nitrogen – reduces yields, and the soil must be well drained. In hot climates buckwheat can be grown only by sowing late in the season, so that it blooms in cooler weather.

►Tapioca flour is a very fine, white powder that works well in gluten free baking. It can replace cornstarch as a thickener for pies, gravies, pudding, dough and sauces and aids in creating a crisp crust and chewy.

description:
Millet grain doesn’t have any gluten contains lots of essential vitamins, minerals, and fiber. This grain has been a staple in many cuisines for years. And while it’s not as popular as rice, wheat, or oats, it’s gaining more recognition all over the world. The reason for this is simple; millet is delicious, nutritious, and very easy to cook.

Food to Live While Millet, also known as White Proso, is the most popular type of this grain. There are about 500 species of plants that are considered millet, but only a few of them used as food. Pearl and foxglove millet also are popular crops. All types of millet are similar in taste and nutritional value. However, experts believe that white millet was domesticated first. Presumably, as a crop, it dates back to around 10,000 BC.


How to Cook White Millet Proso

Hulled whole grain millet has a rich nutty and mildly sweet flavor. Because of this, the grain tastes fantastic in a variety of sweet and savory dishes. In fact, replacing grains in the recipe with this one can make the dish taste much better.

There are many ways to use millet; it is easy to cook; hulled millet doesn’t need pre-soaking and cooks in less than 30 minutes.

Try to roast dry grain in a pan or skillet for about 5 minutes and add water or broth. Use two parts of liquid per 1 part of the grain. Increase the amount of water to three parts if you want to enjoy pure millet taste in a porridge.

After adding water, bring the pot to a boil and turn down the heat to simmer right away. Do not often stir as hulled millet grain is very tender. Let it simmer for about fifteen minutes, so all water is absorbed. Then, let the pot sit covered for ten minutes and fluff up the cooked grain using a fork.

The Barnyard millet (Echinochloa frumantacea) is a wild seed and not a grain, mainly grown in the hilly areas of Uttaranchal, India. The barnyard millet is the fastest growing crop, which can produce ripe grains within 45 days from the sowing time under optimal weather conditions.
The millets have a hard cellulosic husk layer that humans cannot digest. The removal of the husk layer becomes the primary task of processing these grains. description: What Is White Jasmine Rice? Organic white jasmine rice is a long grain type of fragrant rice native to Thailand. It gets its name because of the subtle flowery scent and color of the polished grains, which are reminiscent of jasmine flowers. It’s the most fragrant rice of its kind and is one of the most popular in the Western world. Food To Live brings this delicious grain to your table with our Organic Jasmine Rice. You can use it to create a great variety of delicious dishes, ranging from stir-fry to pudding. Due to its pleasant flowery aroma and mildly-nutty flavor, white jasmine rice can benefit any dish when replacing other rice varieties. This particular type of grain is a traditional ingredient in Thai cuisine. It’s also a staple food in Vietnam, Cambodia, and Laos. Organic Jasmine Rice from Food To Live Food To Live Organic Jasmine Rice bulk pack contains high-quality white rice you’ll be able to enjoy in a variety of ways. This product is versatile and can be used in both sweet and savory dishes. In fact, the natural sweet flavor of organic white jasmine rice makes it a good choice for desserts. As it’s rather soft compared to other long grain rice varieties, you can make an excellent pudding with it. Difference Between Basmati and White Jasmine Rice Both basmati and jasmine rice are types of fragrant long grain rice. They are very popular in Thailand, India, China, and other Eastern countries. These grains can be used interchangeably, but white jasmine rice has a milder more flowery flavor and aroma. Basmati is a firmer, longer, and less sticky grain. It requires soaking for at least 30 minutes before cooking, while white jasmine rice can be cooked after a short rinse. The best way to cooking organic jasmine rice is steaming, but you can also boil it on the stove using 1:1 or 1:1.5 proportions of grain and water. description:
Millet grain doesn’t have any gluten contains lots of essential vitamins, minerals, and fiber. This grain has been a staple in many cuisines for years. And while it’s not as popular as rice, wheat, or oats, it’s gaining more recognition all over the world. The reason for this is simple; millet is delicious, nutritious, and very easy to cook.

Food to Live While Millet, also known as White Proso, is the most popular type of this grain. There are about 500 species of plants that are considered millet, but only a few of them used as food. Pearl and foxglove millet also are popular crops. All types of millet are similar in taste and nutritional value. However, experts believe that white millet was domesticated first. Presumably, as a crop, it dates back to around 10,000 BC.


How to Cook White Millet Proso

Hulled whole grain millet has a rich nutty and mildly sweet flavor. Because of this, the grain tastes fantastic in a variety of sweet and savory dishes. In fact, replacing grains in the recipe with this one can make the dish taste much better.

There are many ways to use millet; it is easy to cook; hulled millet doesn’t need pre-soaking and cooks in less than 30 minutes.

Try to roast dry grain in a pan or skillet for about 5 minutes and add water or broth. Use two parts of liquid per 1 part of the grain. Increase the amount of water to three parts if you want to enjoy pure millet taste in a porridge.

After adding water, bring the pot to a boil and turn down the heat to simmer right away. Do not often stir as hulled millet grain is very tender. Let it simmer for about fifteen minutes, so all water is absorbed. Then, let the pot sit covered for ten minutes and fluff up the cooked grain using a fork.

description:
Organic Rye brings one of the most ancient and revered grains to your table. People have been cultivating this grain for over 4000 years. It spread from what the lands currently known as Turkey all over the Middle East and Europe. Organic rye berries are nutritious, delicious, and extremely good for you.


Nutrition Data
Organic rye berries contain lots of B vitamins and a variety of minerals:

Manganese
Phosphorus
Zinc
Magnesium
Iron
Copper

Organic rye berries are extremely rich in dietary fiber and protein.

Due to fiber and overall high nutritional value, organic rye berries will be a good addition to a weight management diet.


How to Cook

Cooking organic rye berries takes a while. If you soak rye grain berries overnight, they will only take about 45 minutes to cook. Otherwise, the process can take about 3 hours.

To cook organic rye berries, you’ll need to use 1 cup of water per ½ cup of dry grains. Be sure to add about ¼ teaspoon of salt.

Drain cooked organic rye berries and serve while they are still hot.

If you plan to use organic rye berries in a stew or other dish that will require them to cook further, drain them while the seeds are firm Organic rye berries, sprouted or not, should be cooked. If you are 100% sure that your sprouts weren’t contaminated by any bacteria, you can eat them as they are. However, rinse them extremely well and drain thoroughly.

Add this kind of sprouts to salads and sandwiches.

Cooked rye berries go well in salads, both warm and cold. They taste good with any type of vegetable.

Organic rye berries are perfect for delicious and healthy baked goods. However, organic rye bread requires yeast to make. Don’t forget that you can mix whole berries into the dough for extra-crunch.


The most important thing is to keep them dry and cool.

description: Organic Wild Rice: Sacred Grain of Native Americans Organic wild rice is a grain that comes from North America. For many centuries it has been the staple food of many Native American peoples. Some of them considered this food sacred and it takes a special place in their cultures even today. Food To Live brings you top-quality Organic Wild Rice grown, harvested, and processed with extreme care. This highly nutritious grain is a delicacy you can enjoy in both sweet and savory dishes. There are four species of wild rice plants today and three of them are native to America. Northern Wild Rice and Wild Rice are cultivated throughout the country. Texas Wild Rice is almost extinct in the wild. This plant has taken a severe blow from the climate change as it’s rapidly losing its natural habitat. Organic wild rice is a water plant and naturally grows only in flowing water. Therefore, droughts are a fatal threat to the grains. In 1951, Gerald and James Godward proved that it can be cultivated commercially by creating the first artificial wild rice paddy. It’s thanks to them today we have wild rice fields in Minnesota and California. Manchurian rice, the only species of the plant native to China, is also almost lost to people. Unlike its North American ‘brother’ this plant is mostly cultivated for its meaty stalk. Local people enjoy it as a vegetable and often discard seeds. Food To Live Certified Organic Wild Rice for Sale Organic, non-GMO Wild Rice from Food To Live is a certified product cultivated using only natural practices. It’s grown, harvested, and processed using the traditional methods, which allow preventing contamination by chemicals. Harvesting of organic wild rice is a rather interesting but exhausting process. The seeds are literally beaten out of the plants with special knockers. Afterward, they are dried and parched. The parching process enhances the delicious flavor of this extraordinary grain.

description:
Buckwheat is a superfood that you may not know about. It’s definitely under-appreciated and under-utilized in the US, but everyone should know how healthy and scrumptious it is!

It is made from roasted groats that are cooked with broth to a texture similar to rice. The dish was brought to America by Russian and Polish immigrants who called it "Kasha" or "Grechka".

It’s also completely gluten free! It’s name is a little deceiving because it’s called buckwheat but there is no relation to wheat – none whatsoever! It’s also just as simple to make as white rice.


Ingredients for Basic Buckwheat:
  • 1 cup toasted buckwheat groats;
  • 1 3/4 cups filtered water;
  • 1-2 Tbsp butter, to taste (I used unsalted butter);
  • 1/2 tsp salt, or to taste (I used sea salt);

How to Cook Buckwheat Kasha

Stove-top Method:

Rinse and drain buckwheat well.

In a medium sauce pan, combine buckwheat with 1¾ cups water, 1 Tbsp butter and ½ tsp salt. Bring to a simmer then cover with a tight fitting lid and simmer on low for 18-20 min. Just like with rice, you should hear hissing while cooking and it will get quiet when done. Stir in additional 1 Tbsp butter if desired.

Rice Cooker Method:

Transfer all ingredients to the rice cooker and set on the white rice setting. When done, add an extra Tbsp of butter if desired and stir in 1-2 tsp water to moisten up the kernels if they seem dry. Serve hot.

description:
GOLDEN CROWN SUSHI RICE

In Japan, sushi rice means the steamed rice that’s flavored with vinegar-based seasonings. Sushi rice has one of the most pleasing textures in the world, which makes it the best, IMO. And the bright pop of vinegar and the sweetness from the sugar added to sushi rice don't hurt anything either.

Perfectly cooked Sushi Rice (酢飯) is fundamental in making authentic sushi and exploring Japanese cooking. Once you’ve mastered perfectly seasoned and fluffy sushi rice, your sushi tastes much better. This authentic sushi rice recipe is easy to make at home.

INGREDIENTS

  • 2 cups uncooked glutinous white rice (sushi rice)
  • 3 cups water
  • ½ cup rice vinegar
  • 1 tablespoon vegetable oil
  • ¼ cup white sugar
  • 1 teaspoon salt

    Step 1 Rinse the rice in a strainer or colander until the water runs clear. Combine with water in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover and cook for 20 minutes. Rice should be tender and water should be absorbed. Cool until cool enough to handle.

    Step 2 In a small saucepan, combine the rice vinegar, oil, sugar and salt. Cook over medium heat until the sugar dissolves. Cool, then stir into the cooked rice. When you pour this in to the rice it will seem very wet. Keep stirring and the rice will dry as it cools.

description:
If you wish to exercise another grain but rice, try our Organic Spelt Berries. This delicious grain has been around for millennia; today, organic farmers are raving about wheat berries because they need fewer chemicals to grow compared to regular bread wheat. Organic Whole Spelt Berries are easy to cook and you can enjoy them in any recipe that calls for grains.

Like all whole grains, organic spelt berries are rich in fiber, B vitamins, and plant protein. Use them as a substitute for rice, even in recipes like risotto. However, unlike most whole grains, spelt wheat berries have a rich nutty flavor. Therefore, they will enhance the taste of any dish and are delicious served as a side on their own.

Please remember that Organic Whole Spelt Berries are a type of wheat; therefore, there is gluten.


How to Cook & Sprout Organic Spelt Berries

Make sure to soak Spelt Berries before cooking, overnight soaking will give you the best results, but if you can’t wait that long, leave them soaking for at least an hour.

Place the berries and water where the Spelt berries soaked in a pot and bring to a boil.

Turn down the heat and let simmer for 1-1 ½ hours.

Season with salt near the end and then drain and use the cooked grain as guided by your recipe.

When cooking spelt wheat berries, use 2 cups of water per 1 cup of grain for a chewier texture. If you need softer grain, use 3 cups of water per cup of dry spelt berries.

If you buy organic spelt berries in bulk, you might want to try not just cooking them but also grind into homemade flour or sprout. Sprouting spelt berries is the same as sprouting any other whole grain. Let them soak, cover, and then rinse and drain in a sprouter.

description: Farro (pronounced FAHR-oh) is one of the oldest cultivated grains on our planet. In fact, history books describe faro as the oldest and original grain domesticated by humans in the Fertile Crescent of the Middle East. The Fertile Crescent is a quarter moon shaped region that stretches from the Mediterranean Sea on the west to the Persian Gulf on the east and is often considered to be the location of the biblical “Garden of Eden”. Farro became the primary grain consumed by the Roman Empire; in fact farro helped fuel the Roman legions’ march across Europe and the Middle East. As new varieties of wheat were discovered or created through hybridization, farro fell out of favor. Today farro is one of several "ancient whole grains" that are being rediscovered by chefs and health conscious consumers around the world. Farro is a great source of vitamins and nutrients, as well as protein and fiber. We are the first company to make imported Italian Farro widely available to mainstream consumer in the United Sates. description:
Organic Rye brings one of the most ancient and revered grains to your table. People have been cultivating this grain for over 4000 years. It spread from what the lands currently known as Turkey all over the Middle East and Europe. Organic rye berries are nutritious, delicious, and extremely good for you.


Nutrition Data
Organic rye berries contain lots of B vitamins and a variety of minerals:

Manganese
Phosphorus
Zinc
Magnesium
Iron
Copper

Organic rye berries are extremely rich in dietary fiber and protein.

Due to fiber and overall high nutritional value, organic rye berries will be a good addition to a weight management diet.


How to Cook

Cooking organic rye berries takes a while. If you soak rye grain berries overnight, they will only take about 45 minutes to cook. Otherwise, the process can take about 3 hours.

To cook organic rye berries, you’ll need to use 1 cup of water per ½ cup of dry grains. Be sure to add about ¼ teaspoon of salt.

Drain cooked organic rye berries and serve while they are still hot.

If you plan to use organic rye berries in a stew or other dish that will require them to cook further, drain them while the seeds are firm Organic rye berries, sprouted or not, should be cooked. If you are 100% sure that your sprouts weren’t contaminated by any bacteria, you can eat them as they are. However, rinse them extremely well and drain thoroughly.

Add this kind of sprouts to salads and sandwiches.

Cooked rye berries go well in salads, both warm and cold. They taste good with any type of vegetable.

Organic rye berries are perfect for delicious and healthy baked goods. However, organic rye bread requires yeast to make. Don’t forget that you can mix whole berries into the dough for extra-crunch.


The most important thing is to keep them dry and cool.

What is Quinoa? Royal Quinoa pronunciation: keen-wa, is a "pseudo-grain" or a gluten and wheat free seed, but typically used as a grain. Royal Quinoa is rich in many nutrients and a great source of protein and fiber for those following a gluten free, vegan or vegetarian diet.

Quinoa was a staple food for the Incas that dates back 3,000 years ago. It was first used for consumption in the Andean region of Bolivia. The Incas called it the “mother grain” and would host ceremonies at the first planting of the season to show respect for all the greatness that the plant provided for them.

During the European conquest, the Spanish colonist disparaged Quinoa as “food for Indians” and suppressed its cultivation. Quinoa flourished once again in the high mountains, over 4,000 meters over the sea level since it is one of few crops that survives high altitude, withstands frost, intense sun and the often-dry conditions that characterized the Andean climate.

منذ عام 1937، تعمل مزارع لوندبرغ العائلية على نمو الأرز الصحي والمذاق الرائع بينما تميل إلى التربة والهواء والماء والحياة البرية بعناية مثلما كانت محاصيلنا الخاصة. يقول بعض الناس إننا غير تقليدية قليلاً. ولكن القيام بالأمور بطريقتنا - بشكل مستدام في كل خطوة - يسمح لنا بصنع طعام أفضل لطاولتك مع ترك عالم أفضل للجيل التالي. نمت مع ممارسات الحفاظ على الأرض، يتم زراعة أكثر من 20 قطعة من الأرز والكينوا لتحقيق أقصى قدر من نكهة كل حبة صغيرة. طويل، قصير، أسود، بني، أبيض، أحمر، وممزوج. كل مجموعة متنوعة تجلب شيئًا مختلفًا على الطاولة حتى تتمكن من الإبداع في المطبخ. استمتع بتنوع أنواع أرز الياسمين الأبيض بكاليفورنيا العضوية من لوندبرغ. مع رائحة زهور خفيفة ونكهة زبدة، فإن أرز الياسمين الأبيض من كاليفورنيا لا يقاوم عمليًا. تلتصق هذه الحبوب الطويلة معًا عند طهيها ولكنها ليست لزجة، لذلك يمكنك تقديمها في الكاري التايلاندي والبيلاف والحلوى التي تتطلب وجود حبات مميزة وملمس ناعم. هل أنت جائع للمزيد؟ ابحث عن الأطباق الجانبية الأخرى ذات المذاق الرائع والمداخل والوجبات الخفيفة والأرز المعبأ والكينوا من مزارع لندبرغ. جيدة من الحبيبات!

description:
WHAT IS QUINOA EXACTLY?

Quinoa is often referred to as a "pseudocereal" (just like buckwheat, amaranth, and chia) because it is technically not a grain but a seed, yet similar to true cereals when it comes to flavor, cooking, and nutritional profile. According to the Whole Grains Council, quinoa is a gluten-free, whole-grain carbohydrate, as well as a whole protein (meaning it contains all nine essential amino acids).

QUINOA NUTRITIONAL FACTS

Overall, quinoa has an incredible nutrition base. Compared with refined grains, whole grains like quinoa are considered better sources of fiber, protein, B vitamins, and iron But aside from these key nutrients, one of the greatest nutrient profiles quinoa can offer is its level of protein. Because protein makes up 15 percent of the grain, as reported by the Grains & Legumes Nutrition Council, quinoa is a high-protein, low-fat grain option. It’s also naturally gluten-free, high in fiber, and provides many key vitamins and minerals, including vitamin B and magnesium.

COOKING INSTRUCTIONS

1) The ratio is 1 cup of uncooked quinoa to under cold water until the water runs clear.

2) Bring rinsed quinoa and liquid to a boil in a medium saucepan. stir occasionally.

3) Reduce heat to maintain a low simmer until tender and most of the liquid has been absorbed in and cook for 15 minutes.
A VALUABLE SOURCE FOR HEALTH

In addition, quinoa is a valuable source of heart-healthy fatty acids, rich in phytonutrients and antioxidants offering powerful anti-inflammatory benefits, Vitamins B and E, as well as minerals such as potassium, phosphorus, magnesium, calcium, and zinc. Its high content of both soluble and insoluble fiber may aid in keeping blood sugar levels balanced and lowering cholesterol levels.

HEALTH BENEFITS OF QUINOA

1) Very Nutritious

2) Very High in Fiber, Much Higher Than Most Grains

3) Gluten-Free

4) Very High in Protein</
